items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 4:04PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 6
inches. Winds gusting 20 to 25 mph along the coast will
gradually decrease through the weekend.

* WHERE...Noatak Valley and Northwest Arctic Coast including
Kivalina.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon. Heaviest snow expected from
Friday night through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could reduce visibility.
items.areas: Noatak Valley; Kivalina and Red Dog Dock

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 30 at 3:35PM AKDT until October 31 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Cordova.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest gusts are expected to be in the
town of Cordova with gusts up to 65 mph for Cordova Airport.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of power outages.
Use caution if you must travel.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 30 at 2:29PM AKDT until October 31 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Unalaska and Nikolski.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest wind gusts will begin this
evening and last through early Saturday morning, then diminish
through the rest of Saturday.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 1:22PM AKDT until October 31 at 12:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 30 at 1:17PM AKDT until October 31 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 2.5 to 3.0 feet above the normal high
tide expected during the Friday afternoon high tide.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast, specifically Hooper Bay.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Beach property and lowest buildings may be impacted.
Multiple high tide cycles above normal may lead to localized
beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels of around 1 to 2 feet above
the normal high tide line are expected along the rest of the
Yukon Delta Coast.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 30 at 12:59PM AKDT until November 1 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:

inches possible. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...The Klondike Highway including White Pass

* WHEN...From 10 AM AKDT Saturday to 9 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Conditions will likely
become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels will start out around 600' early
Saturday morning but are expected to rise to around 1,500' by mid
day Saturday. This will limit snow accumulat
items.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. For the latest road conditions where
available call 511 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 11:59AM AKDT until October 30 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Visibility one half mile or less at times.
Total snow accumulations 10 to 15 inches.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The heaviest snow is expected through late
this afternoon. Warming temperatures through this afternoon will
lead to a changeover to rain for lower elevations of the pass. The
top of the pass will likely remain all snow.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.
